안녕하다.gloss: to be well, to be at peace

meanings.en: to be well, to be at peace
meanings.note: Mainly used in greetings like '안녕하세요'.

examples.trans: Hello? (Are you well?)
I hope everyone is well.
Did you hear about this by our president?
I was busy today because of by our president.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
Did you hear about this not fond of?
I was busy today because of not fond of.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
Let's got drunk and together today.
I worked hard to got drunk and yesterday too.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning 'together', often pronounced 가치.

examples.trans: Let's go together.
Let's go together. (2)

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: used before a verb to tell someone to stop an ongoing action

examples.trans: Stop worrying now.
I'm so full I'll stop eating.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.
I want to did you send? right now.
How about trying to did you send? together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to like, to be fond of
meanings.note: Takes an object marked with 을/를.

examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?
I like listening to music.

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So let's go.
Therefore it is good.

meanings.note: native Korean numeral; 둘이 means 'the two of them'

examples.trans: The two of us work together.
Two coffees, please.

meanings.note: Descriptive verb (adjective); the thing disliked takes the subject marker 이/가.

examples.trans: I really dislike rainy days.
You hate waking up early in the morning, right?
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 넌 전화기를 놓고 가면 어떡하냐, 나는 꼼장어도 추가하려고.
examples.trans: How could you walk out leaving your phone behind—anyway, I came down to add grilled hagfish too.
Here the word for 'your phone' is key.

놓다.gloss: to put, to place, to leave

meanings.en: to put, to place, to leave
meanings.note: Often used as an auxiliary verb to indicate leaving something in a certain state.

examples.trans: Please place it on the desk.
I left the door open.

meanings.en: what to do, how to act
meanings.note: Contraction of 어떻게 하다.

examples.trans: What should we do?
What should we do? (2)

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 넌 전화기를 놓고 가면 어떡하냐, 나는 꼼장어도 추가하려고.
examples.trans: How could you walk out leaving your phone behind—anyway, I came down to add grilled hagfish too.
Here the word for 'grilled hagfish too' is key.

추가하다.gloss: intending to add to the order

meanings.en: intending to add to the order
meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 넌 전화기를 놓고 가면 어떡하냐, 나는 꼼장어도 추가하려고.
examples.trans: How could you walk out leaving your phone behind—anyway, I came down to add grilled hagfish too.
This expression comes from 'intending to add to the order'.

meanings.note: refers to a previously mentioned or specific day

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
I don't have time that day.

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

examples.trans: Hey, you there, just a moment!
How is the atmosphere there?
Did you hear about this corporate card?
I was busy today because of corporate card.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (num).

examples.text: 안 난다니까, 포장마차에서 뭘 먹었길래 7만 원이 나오냐?
examples.trans: I told you I do not remember—what on earth did we eat at a street tent to rack up seventy thousand won?
Here the word for 'seventy thousand' is key.

meanings.note: Bound noun used with Sino-Korean numbers to state prices in South Korean won.

examples.trans: I only have a thousand won.
That is ten thousand won in total.
Let's pay off together today.
I worked hard to pay off yesterday too.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Do you really not remember anything from the street tent?
Here the word for 'at the street snack tent?' is key.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나? 나 뮤직뱅크 탁예진 피디 기억나지?
examples.trans: Me? You remember Music Bank producer Tak Ye-jin, right?
This expression comes from 'you remember, right?'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 만약에 기억을 하는데도 아무 반응을 안 보이고 있는 거라면, 준모가 그 진심을 편집해버렸단 얘기 아닐까?
examples.trans: If he remembers everything and still shows no reaction, does that not mean Joon-mo edited out those feelings?
This expression comes from 'edited right out'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'nights' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 선배님이 편집해버린 그날 밤 예진 선배님 이야기 기억나세요?
examples.trans: Do you remember Senior Ye-jin's confession from that night—the one you edited out?
Here the word for 'story, confession' is key.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
